newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: PRIVATISATION SEES RISE IN ZAMBIAN STOCK TRADING.
newsitem.headline: PRIVATISATION SEES RISE IN ZAMBIAN STOCK TRADING.

text.p: Zambia's stock trading rose markedly in 1996 as the privatisation of state-run enterprises increased floatations, the Lusaka stock exchange said on Wednesday.
It said traded volume rose to 241,381,900 kwacha with turnover at $2,643,146.
Volumes in 1994 were 3,934,020 with a turnover of $368,384.
"Trading activity, volume of shares and turnover increased markedly in 1996 compared to 1994 and 1995 when the market was just starting," exchange general manager Charles Mate said.
"The upward trend is the result of greater awareness in the general public as well as the growth of the stock market, driven by floatations from the privatisation programme," he added.

Metal Fabricators of Zambia, British Petroleum (Zambia), National Breweries and Northern Breweries were among the companies privatised with a significant component reserved for floatation through the Zambia Privatisation Trust Fund.
Mate said Zambia Breweries was expected to be listed between April and May, bringing to six the number of companies listed on the exchange.
"The exchange would like to see the listing of BP Zambia, ZAMEFA and National Breweries in 1997," he said.
In addition, a number of local institutions were working on establishing the first unit trust in the country this year, Mate said.
